prompt: Why kill a healthy primary on purpose?

choices.why: A rehearsal has nothing to do with the WAL's size.

choices.text: Because Patroni needs it to work
choices.why: Patroni works without rehearsals; you just do not know that it does.
Right: to choose when the first real failover happens, on a day when finding a problem costs nothing.
That is lesson 7's drill.

prompt: Match each finding a rehearsal can make with the lesson it echoes.

pairs.left: A setting right on two nodes and wrong on the third
An application that keeps a stale address
A runbook naming a renamed server

right_distractors: A slot holding too much log

prompt: Why is the expectation written down as a number before the rehearsal?

choices.text: So that the result can surprise you
choices.why: Right: a result compared with nothing confirms whatever happened.
The reason is the comparison, not an audit.
The ttl is configuration, not the expectation.

choices.text: So the rehearsal can be skipped next time
choices.why: It is repeated on a schedule.

prompt: Why must a rehearsal refuse to start on a cluster missing a node?
hint: How many failures can it absorb?

choices.why: It would fail over; the risk is what follows.
It routes to however many are up.

choices.text: The script cannot count to two
choices.why: The script counts fine; the plan forbids it.

choices.text: Killing the leader would leave one node
choices.why: Right: then the rehearsal is the incident.

prompt: Put the rehearsal's plan in the order it is used.
hint: Paper first, failure in the middle.
items: Compare the results with the expectation
trap: Checking the abort criteria after causing the failure is checking too late.

prompt: Where does `rehearsal.sh` read the cluster's state from?

choices.why: It asks patronictl, which reads etcd.
Right: parsed by a few lines of Python.
That shows routing, not lag.
patronictl summarises that.

prompt: `export PG___ = 5` makes every libpq connection give up after five seconds.
The first version of the script met the lag `unknown` and kept going. Why is that worse than having no check?
hint: What does a check that passes make people believe?

choices.why: Speed is not the issue.
Right: and it guards nothing; a guard that fails open reports a healthy run on a broken cluster.
Memory is not the issue.
It ran as ana.

prompt: What lag, in MB, does the fixed script count for a replica whose lag it cannot read?
hint: A number that can only stop it.

prompt: With `pg3` stopped, what did the rehearsal do?

choices.why: That is what the first version effectively risked.
Starting nodes is not its job before the run.

choices.text: Waited for pg3 to come back
choices.why: It refuses, it does not wait.
Right: printed ABORT and exited 1 before touching anything; two healthy members out of three.

prompt: The leader was killed at 03:14:10 and the first order after the failure succeeded at 03:14:41. How many seconds without orders?
16 orders were reported `ok` and the table gained 16 rows. What does that confirm?

choices.why: Right: no order reported as saved went missing, as the plan expected.
It took about 31.
pg1 rejoined as a replica.

choices.text: HAProxy sent 16 orders to each node
choices.why: All went to the primary.

prompt: What did the first run of the rehearsal find?

choices.why: It promoted a new leader as usual.
It only inserts.
Right: left waiting with no server behind it, held open by HAProxy for up to its 30-minute timeout, with no limit in psql.

choices.text: etcd lost the leader key permanently
choices.why: etcd worked.

prompt: Why is the hung connection worse for a real application than for the rehearsal?

choices.why: The database is fine.
HAProxy kept running.

choices.text: It has no effect on applications
choices.why: Applications hold workers on connections.
Right: stuck connections exhaust the workers after the failover ends; the shop goes down after the database has recovered.

prompt: Put the steps of making rehearsals more real in the lesson's order.
hint: From what loses nothing to production.
items: A killed leader in a test environment
The same with the real application and traffic
A killed leader in production, at an agreed time
trap: Each step is only safe once the one before has passed.

prompt: A rehearsal found nothing wrong. What happens to its results?

choices.text: They are discarded, since nothing failed
choices.why: Nothing failing is a result.
It is repeated on a schedule.
Right: written down as evidence; the next rehearsal is compared with them.
Nothing suggests a change.

prompt: A team wants its first rehearsal to be a killed leader in production next Monday. What does the lesson suggest instead?

choices.why: Right: a switchover first, then a killed leader in a test environment; each step earns the next.

choices.text: Skip the abort criteria to save time
choices.why: They are what keeps it a rehearsal.

choices.text: Do it without telling anybody, to make it realistic
choices.why: Everybody affected is told before and after.
Restores have their own drill; the failover still needs one.
